hpi_details: 60M presenting with rapidly growing 5cm cervical lymph node mass, fevers, and night sweats. Biopsy confirms aggressive CD20+ diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
ideas: He thinks the lump is just a badly swollen gland or deep cyst caused by a stubborn throat infection he caught a few weeks ago.

available_results.value: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, CD20 positive

clinical_knowledge.topic: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL) is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes prompt histologic confirmation, full staging with PET-CT, and initiation of curative-intent R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy given the aggressive but chemosensitive nature of this lymphoma, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: rapidly enlarging painless neck mass, drenching sweats, and weight loss
Key HPI features: 60M presenting with rapidly growing 5cm cervical lymph node mass, fevers, and night sweats. Biopsy confirms aggressive CD20+ diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: Temp 38.1C, HR 92, BP 126/78, unintentional weight loss of 8kg over 2 months. Firm, non-tender, rubbery 5cm right cervical lymph node; no other palpable lymphadenopathy; no hepatosplenomegaly on exam. Bloods: mild normocytic anemia, LDH markedly elevated (poor prognostic marker), ESR elevated. Excisional lymph node biopsy with immunohistochemistry confirms CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
Relevant background/PMH: No significant chronic medical history
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL).
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Hodgkin lymphoma without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Rapid growth over weeks — this pace is itself a warning sign of an aggressive lymphoma.
management_principles: Complete staging workup: whole-body PET-CT, bone marrow biopsy, LDH, and HIV/Hepatitis B and C serologies (Hepatitis B screening is essential before Rituximab due to reactivation risk)
Obtain baseline echocardiogram (LVEF) before anthracycline-containing chemotherapy
Initiate curative-intent R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Vincristine, Prednisone) every 21 days for 6 cycles
Give tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis (allopurinol and IV hydration) before the first cycle given the tumor's rapid proliferation rate
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma DLBCL: rapidly enlarging painless neck mass, drenching sweats, and weight loss. 60M presenting with rapidly growing 5cm cervical lymph node mass, fevers, and night sweats. Biopsy confirms aggressive CD20+ diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: Temp 38.1C, HR 92, BP 126/78, unintentional weight loss of 8kg over 2 months. Firm, non-tender, rubbery 5cm right cervical lymph node; no other palpable lymphadenopathy; no hepatosplenomegaly on exam. Bloods: mild normocytic anemia, LDH markedly elevated (poor prognostic marker), ESR elevated. Excisional lymph node biopsy with immunohistochemistry confirms CD20-positive diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
reference_soap.assessment: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL), an aggressive but potentially curable non-Hodgkin lymphoma, presenting with a rapidly enlarging cervical mass and B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss).
reference_soap.plan: 1. Complete staging workup: whole-body PET-CT, bone marrow biopsy, LDH, and HIV/Hepatitis B and C serologies before starting Rituximab. 2. Obtain baseline echocardiogram (LVEF) given planned anthracycline (doxorubicin) exposure. 3. Initiate curative-intent R-CHOP chemoimmunotherapy (Rituximab, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin, Vincristine, Prednisone) every 21 days for 6 cycles. 4. Give tumor lysis syndrome prophylaxis (allopurinol and IV hydration) before cycle 1 given the tumor's rapid proliferation rate. 5. Urgent referral to hematology-oncology; counsel patient on the aggressive-but-curable nature of DLBCL and expected treatment course.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical features and diagnostic criteria of Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma DLBCL
Formulate prioritized differential diagnosis for rapidly enlarging painless neck mass, drenching sweats, and weight loss
Select appropriate laboratory and imaging studies for hematology_oncology
Implement evidence-based acute and long-term management strategies

teaching.one_liner: The most common aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma, presenting as a rapidly enlarging lymph node mass with B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) — fast-growing but often curable with chemotherapy.
red_flags: Rapid growth over weeks — this pace is itself a warning sign of an aggressive lymphoma

must_ask.say: How quickly has this lump grown — over weeks?
Have you had fevers, drenching night sweats, or weight loss?
Where is the lump, and is it painful?
When did you first notice it?
Any fatigue or loss of appetite?

history.answer: I found a lump on the right side of my neck about a month ago, and it has been growing very quickly.
I first noticed it about four weeks ago as a small bump, but it expanded to the size of a golf ball in just a few weeks.
It is on the right side of my neck, just below my jawline.
There is just this one large lump on my neck, and I have not felt any others under my arms or in my groin.
No, it does not hurt at all, even when I press directly on it.
No, it stays right where it is when I swallow water or stick out my tongue.
No, eating meals does not change its size or make it tender at all.
No, I haven't had any colds, sore throat, dental problems, or skin infections lately.
Yes, I have been feeling warm and having low-grade fevers on and off over the past month.
Yes, I have been waking up with drenching night sweats that soak through my pajamas and sheets almost every night.
Yes, I weighed myself and I have lost about 8 kilograms over the past two months without trying to diet.
No, I can swallow normally, my voice has not changed, and I am not having any trouble breathing.
No ear pain, no stuffy nose, and no nosebleeds.
No, I haven't felt any heart palpitations, hand tremors, or unusual sensitivity to hot or cold temperatures.
No, I have never had tuberculosis, and to my knowledge I have never been exposed to anyone who had it.
No, I don't own any pets and I haven't been around cats or had any animal scratches.
No, I never had any radiation treatments to my head or neck as a child.
I have felt more exhausted than usual lately, but I haven't had any severe skin itching.
No, I haven't noticed any unusual bruising, bleeding gums, or nosebleeds.
No, my stomach feels normal and I don't have any fullness or swelling there.
I thought it was just a swollen gland or a deep infection from a nasty cold I had a few weeks back.
I'm really worried that if this turns into something drawn-out, I won't be able to keep working full-time at my job.
I was hoping you could prescribe a strong antibiotic or drain the swelling so I can get back to normal.
I have always been healthy and don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I do not take any prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, or herbal supplements.
No, I do not have any known allergies to medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used any tobacco products.
I only drink socially, maybe a beer or a glass of wine once or twice a month.
I work full-time as an office manager and live at home with my wife.
There is no family history of lymphoma, thyroid cancer, or any other cancers that I know of.

exam.finding: Temperature 38.1°C, blood pressure 126/78 mmHg, heart rate 92 beats/min, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
Alert, appears mildly fatigued and diaphoretic, with a visible right neck mass.
Mild conjunctival pallor present; sclerae are clear and non-icteric.
Oral cavity and pharynx are clear with normal tonsils and no mucosal ulcers or infection.
Firm, rubbery, non-tender right cervical lymph node measuring about 5 cm; no other palpable cervical or supraclavicular nodes.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, non-tender, without nodules, and moves normally with swallowing.
No palpable axillary lymph nodes bilaterally; normal breast tissue.
Clear breath sounds bilaterally with good air entry and no wheezing or crackles.
Regular rhythm with mild tachycardia; normal S1 and S2 with no murmurs or rubs.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender; liver and spleen are not palpable.
No palpable inguinal lymphadenopathy and no hernias identified bilaterally.
